description_full: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. through its subsidiaries, provides educational and value-added telecommunication services in the People's Republic of China. It operates through four segments: Educational Services and Test Preparation Courses; Private Label Products and Livestreaming E-Commerce; Overseas Study Consulting Services; and Educational Materials and Distribution. The company offers test preparation courses to students taking language and entrance exams used by educational institutions. It also provides non-academic tutoring courses; intelligent learning systems and devices to offer a digital learning experience for students; and overseas studies consulting services. In addition, the company develops and edits educational materials for language training and test preparation; online education services through the Koolearn.com platform; sells private label products; and engages in livestreaming e-commerce business. Further, it offers educational programs, services, and products to students through schools, learning centers, and bookstores, as well as through its online learning platforms. It distributes its educational materials through various distribution channels, including bookstores and third-party distributors. New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: New Oriental Education & Techno is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $8.5B market cap on $5.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +24% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 8% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $780M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield of 3.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.3% of the shares.
